  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between the planks (kerashim) and the mitzvos, noting that the planks represent spiritual service within man which cannot draw down Ein Sof, while the mitzvos performed in physicality draw down the very Essence (Atzmus).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And with this the precise language in the maamar regarding the difference between the planks and the mitzvos will be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">that the planks are in the manner of</t>
    <t s="3">(only in the manner of)</t>
    <t s="4">the mitzvos, and also that regarding the planks the language “join” is used and not “draw down.”</t>
    <t s="5">For behold, according to what was stated above in the previous sections, the service of the planks is a spiritual service within man,</t>
    <t s="6">and as it is explained</t>
    <t s="7">regarding the matter of the service of the sacrifices, that a person must serve with the fire of the Nefesh HaElokis, which is the supernal fire within man, and with the fire of the Nefesh HaBahamis, which is the mundane fire within man,</t>
    <t s="8">and he must refine the Nefesh HaBahamis in the particular levels within it, as explained above regarding the matter of ox, lamb, goat,</t>
    <t s="9">and therefore, although the service is in this physical world, nevertheless relative to this physical world itself, this is a spiritual service and not a physical service,</t>
    <t s="10">and it is not the matter of actual action</t>
    <t s="11">(about which they say “action above”),</t>
    <t s="12">and it is not the hardest and strongest dust.</t>
    <t s="13">And this is also what the Baal Shem Tov, his soul in Eden, said,</t>
    <t s="14">that a “keresh” (plank) is a person, whose matter is to join and connect worlds with Elokus,</t>
    <t s="15">and as it is brought in Tikkunei Zohar</t>
    <t s="16">on the verse</t>
    <t s="17">“ten cubits the length of the plank,” this is the measure of the body of a person,</t>
    <t s="18">that a person has ten powers: seven midos and three mochin,</t>
    <t s="19">and this is the matter of the service of the planks, which is the service of the Nefesh HaElokis and Nefesh HaBahamis,</t>
    <t s="20">to make from physical things,</t>
    <t s="21">the folly of the side of impurity,</t>
    <t s="22">and to transform them into the folly of holiness.</t>
    <t s="23">And since the service of the planks is a spiritual service within man,</t>
    <t s="24">therefore it is impossible to draw down Ein Sof through it,</t>
    <t s="25">because the drawing down of the light is from the Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="26">and the drawing down from the Atzmus is only through the service that is in the very lowest level,</t>
    <t s="27">and that is the fulfillment of the mitzvos in physicality,</t>
    <t s="28">and therefore regarding the mitzvos the language “draw down” is used.</t>
    <t s="29">Because the mitzvos are in physicality,</t>
    <t s="30">and as explained by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe of the hillula, in several maamarim,</t>
    <t s="31">that even the mitzvos of the duties of the heart,</t>
    <t s="32">behold, the commandment regarding them is that they be felt in the physical flesh, in the brain and heart.</t>
    <t s="33">And like with fear, which must be a contraction in the brain and heart physically,</t>
    <t s="34">and likewise with comprehension, there must be additional lines and wrinkles in the physical brain from the contemplation and depth in the comprehension of Torah,</t>
    <t s="35">and likewise in the totality of service, which must be with delight from his service to his Creator,</t>
    <t s="36">behold, the delight must add fatness, as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="37">“Good news fattens the bone,”</t>
    <t s="38">physical fatness in the physical flesh.</t>
    <t s="39">And this is what is said in the maamar, that the planks are analogous to the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="40">that through the planks the very high is also drawn down, but not the very highest,</t>
    <t s="41">rather, specifically through the mitzvos the very highest, which is the Atzmus, is drawn down.</t>
    <t s="42">For this is the matter of the mitzvos, that they are drawn from the Atzmus and connect Ein Sof, blessed be He, with the worlds,</t>
    <t s="43">and through a person fulfilling the mitzvos, behold initially he connects them with the worlds,</t>
    <t s="44">which is at the beginning of the service through spiritual service, which is the service of the planks,</t>
    <t s="45">and afterwards</t>
    <t s="46">(through their fulfillment in physicality)</t>
    <t s="47">he connects them with the Atzmus.</t>
    <t s="48">And it is in the manner of what we find in Torah, that Dovid would connect the supernal Torah with the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="49">behold, so it is also with the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="50">that before their performance,</t>
    <t s="51">in the blessing over the mitzvos we say “Who sanctified us with His mitzvos,”</t>
    <t s="52">with His mitzvos that were already drawn down in supernal kindness, and he draws them upon himself and connects them in the worlds,</t>
    <t s="53">and through his performance of the mitzvos, behold also the Holy One, blessed be He, nods His head,</t>
    <t s="54">which is the drawing down of the Atzmus,</t>
    <t s="55">and likewise with Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, reads and reviews opposite him,</t>
    <t s="56">and likewise in all matters, the Holy One, blessed be He, does measure for measure,</t>
    <t s="57">that what He commands Israel to do, He does Himself,</t>
    <t s="58">meaning that through the action of a Jewish person, he draws them down anew and with added power from the Atzmus.</t>
    <t s="59">And this is what the Maggid said</t>
    <t s="60">on the verse</t>
    <t s="61">“And you shall keep My statutes and My judgments, which a person shall do and live by them,”</t>
    <t s="62">that “My statutes” (chukosai) is thought, which is a unique garment like the letters of engraving,</t>
    <t s="63">“My judgments” (mishpatai) is speech, as it is said “the word of the king is dominion,”</t>
    <t s="64">“a king establishes the land through judgment,”</t>
    <t s="65">“which a person shall do,”</t>
    <t s="66">this is the matter of action, which is the purpose,</t>
    <t s="67">and through this “and live by them,”</t>
    <t s="68">that through the service in thought, and drawing down from thought through speech to the aspect of action,</t>
    <t s="69">behold through this “and live by them,”</t>
    <t s="70">that he draws down life into the mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="71">And this is the matter of the service of the planks, which is a spiritual service within man,</t>
    <t s="72">that through this he comes to the fulfillment of the mitzvos in physicality,</t>
    <t s="73">behold through this they draw down the Atzmus and connect it in the worlds,</t>
    <t s="74">and like the language of the maamar, “roof and floor as one literally,”</t>
    <t s="75">that in the created being, the true being will be revealed.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the hint of the letter Kuf, whose left leg extends downward, representing the need to cut off the klipah's reed (kaneh) to transform it into the letter Hei, leading to the future revelation of "Hinei Elokeinu."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, the maamar continues</t>
    <t s="2">with an explanation of the hint of the letter Kuf, whose left leg extends downward to the very bottom,</t>
    <t s="3">that in general it is what is written</t>
    <t s="4">“Rebuke the beast of the reed,”</t>
    <t s="5">that the matter of “reed” (kaneh) is a long reed that extends downward,</t>
    <t s="6">and it is the male of the klipah,</t>
    <t s="7">and “beast of the reed” (chayas kaneh) is the female of the klipah, the aspect of Malchus of the klipah,</t>
    <t s="8">that receives from the male,</t>
    <t s="9">and one must cut them off,</t>
    <t s="10">this is “rebuke the beast of the reed.”</t>
    <t s="11">And in the service of man, the male of the klipah is the matter of the impure midos,</t>
    <t s="12">and the aspect of Malchus of the klipah is the matter of becoming a doormat that is trampled, etc., and it is the acceptance of the yoke of the side of impurity,</t>
    <t s="13">and there must be “rebuke the beast of the reed,” that one must cut off the reed of the Kuf and break the pride of the tyrants,</t>
    <t s="14">and through cutting off the reed of the Kuf, a Hei is made from it,</t>
    <t s="15">and then it is the word “Hinei” (behold).</t>
    <t s="16">For “Hinei” indicates revelation,</t>
    <t s="17">that revelation is the matter of holiness,</t>
    <t s="18">and therefore in the future, when all matters of holiness that are in hiddenness will be revealed,</t>
    <t s="19">that they will be seen tangibly with physical eyes,</t>
    <t s="20">it is written</t>
    <t s="21">“And it shall be said on that day, ‘Behold, this is our God,’”</t>
    <t s="22">and the revelation of the future is through the service of the present,</t>
    <t s="23">and as explained in the maamar in the previous sections</t>
    <t s="24">and also mentioned in this section in headings,</t>
    <t s="25">that it is the service of transforming darkness into light and bitterness into sweetness,</t>
    <t s="26">that they transform the side of impurity and make from it good and holiness,</t>
    <t s="27">and particularly when there are concealments and hidden things and trials, and nevertheless he is not affected by this at all,</t>
    <t s="28">and on the contrary, through the trials he strengthens himself with added power and added fortitude to serve his service,</t>
    <t s="29">behold through this he transforms from the folly of the side of impurity to the folly of holiness,</t>
    <t s="30">and through this there will be the revelation of the future,</t>
    <t s="31">“And it shall be said on that day, ‘Behold, this is our God… this,’”</t>
    <t s="32">twice “this,”</t>
    <t s="33">that the aspect of “I am Hashem, I have not changed” will be revealed,</t>
    <t s="34">and it is specifically through the service of the present in physicality.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the mitzvos are like planting seeds specifically in the physical earth, and through this service in the lowest world, the essential self-elevation of the King is revealed, which is the eternal love from the Essence beyond all limitations.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And the matter is as explained at length by the holy Tzemach Tzedek</t>
    <t s="2">on the verse</t>
    <t s="3">“Those who come, Yaakov will take root, Israel will blossom and flower,”</t>
    <t s="4">that the mitzvos are called by the name “planting,”</t>
    <t s="5">and just as with physical planting, the planting must be specifically in the earth, and then specifically there will be blossoming, etc.,</t>
    <t s="6">so too with the planting of the mitzvos, in order for them to effect their effect, which is what is said “will blossom and flower,”</t>
    <t s="7">and it is the future revelation which will be “Behold, this is our God,”</t>
    <t s="8">it is specifically through planting the mitzvos in the physical earth.</t>
    <t s="9">And it is in two matters.</t>
    <t s="10">Both from the perspective of the mitzvos themselves, that they are clothed in physicality as above,</t>
    <t s="11">and from the perspective of the serving person, the mitzvos were given to the soul specifically in a body,</t>
    <t s="12">not to the soul as it is above, and not to angels, but specifically to the soul as it is in the physical body,</t>
    <t s="13">behold, specifically in this is the planting of the seed of the mitzvos, through which the blossoming, etc., occurs.</t>
    <t s="14">And as explained there regarding the matter of drawing down the self-elevation, which is His Essence and Being,</t>
    <t s="15">“There is no king without a nation,”</t>
    <t s="16">from the term “faint ones” (omamos) and separate ones,</t>
    <t s="17">and therefore the drawing down of kingship and self-elevation is not through the angels, and certainly not through the souls as they are above, because they are in nullification, as it is said</t>
    <t s="18">“As Hashem, the God of Israel, lives, before Whom I stand,”</t>
    <t s="19">but rather,</t>
    <t s="20">the drawing down of kingship and self-elevation is through the service of the souls as they are below, clothed in a physical body,</t>
    <t s="21">and in this world, where there are two paths, as it is said</t>
    <t s="22">“See, I have set before you… and it is possible to choose, heaven forbid, also the opposite,”</t>
    <t s="23">behold, this is the aspect of “faint ones” and separate ones, through which is the revelation of kingship and self-elevation,</t>
    <t s="24">which is above all lights and revelations,</t>
    <t s="25">and it is the aspect of “I am Hashem, I have not changed.”</t>
    <t s="26">And although “I am Hashem, I have not changed” is constant, for this is the true reality,</t>
    <t s="27">nevertheless, in order for this aspect to be in tangible revelation, as it is written</t>
    <t s="28">“Behold… this,” each one pointing with a finger,</t>
    <t s="29">behold, the tangible revelation will be specifically in the future, and it is specifically through the service now below in physicality.</t>
    <t s="30">And the matter is as explained by the holy Rebbe Maharash, his soul in Eden,</t>
    <t s="31">on the verse</t>
    <t s="32">“With an eternal love I have loved you, therefore I have drawn you with kindness,”</t>
    <t s="33">that it is brought in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu,</t>
    <t s="34">that the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel—</t>
    <t s="35">lest you say it is a love of three years,</t>
    <t s="36">of ten years, or of one hundred years,</t>
    <t s="37">it is not so,</t>
    <t s="38">but rather,</t>
    <t s="39">“With an eternal love I have loved you,”</t>
    <t s="40">and the holy Rebbe Maharash, his soul in Eden, explains in the continuation of “Mayim Rabim”</t>
    <t s="41">that “olam” (world/eternity) is a term for eternity.</t>
    <t s="42">And this is “eternal love,” an eternal love.</t>
    <t s="43">And this does not contradict what is said in many places</t>
    <t s="44">regarding “eternal love” (ahavas olam) that it is lower in level than “great love” (ahavah rabbah),</t>
    <t s="45">and here it is explained that “eternal love” is the most exalted love, above which there is none,</t>
    <t s="46">he explains regarding this,</t>
    <t s="47">that there are two meanings of “olam”: eternity and world, and there are two worlds,</t>
    <t s="48">and as it is said</t>
    <t s="49">“Blessed is Hashem, the God of Israel, from the world and until the world.”</t>
    <t s="50">For although there are many worlds without end, as it is said</t>
    <t s="51">“and countless worlds,” do not read “alamos” (worlds) but “olamos” (worlds),</t>
    <t s="52">nevertheless, in general they are divided into two general categories,</t>
    <t s="53">the revealed world and the hidden world.</t>
    <t s="54">For the revealed world is in measure, limit, and great contraction,</t>
    <t s="55">and when love comes from contemplation of the light that is in measure, limit, and contraction of the world,</t>
    <t s="56">which in general is the aspect of the immanent (Memaleh Kol Almin), and from this comes love,</t>
    <t s="57">behold, since the love comes from something measured, limited, and contracted,</t>
    <t s="58">therefore it is a contracted love and lower than “great love,”</t>
    <t s="59">in contrast, the hidden world is above measurement and limit,</t>
    <t s="60">and in the manner of what is brought in the Gemara</t>
    <t s="61">regarding something hidden from the eye, that blessing rests upon it,</t>
    <t s="62">meaning that it has no limitations.</t>
    <t s="63">And this is the matter of “eternal love” from the term “eternity,” which is higher in level not only from the aspect of “eternal love” of limitation of the aspect of the immanent, but also from the aspect of the transcendent (Sovev).</t>
    <t s="64">For this is the matter of love of three years, ten years, and one hundred years,</t>
    <t s="65">that the Elokus life-force as it is in limitation in the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah is the matter of three years,</t>
    <t s="66">for since in each world there is the matter of world, year, soul, therefore the three worlds are called by the name “three years,”</t>
    <t s="67">love of ten years is in the aspect of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="68">for in Atzilus it is the matter of ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="69">the aspect of ten years.</t>
    <t s="70">And it is above BYA, for in Atzilus there are ten Sefiros without a “what” (b'li mah),</t>
    <t s="71">that although they are ten Sefiros—ten and not nine, ten and not eleven—nevertheless they are without a “what,” and it is above BYA,</t>
    <t s="72">for in order for there to be a drawing down to BYA from Atzilus, it is through the parsa,</t>
    <t s="73">and Atzilus is from the term “etzlo” (near Him) and close,</t>
    <t s="74">and is called the world of unity.</t>
    <t s="75">But nevertheless, even Atzilus is in limitation, and it is not the ultimate love.</t>
    <t s="76">Love of one hundred years is the light as it is in the aspect of Kesser, which is above Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="77">and all the worlds of Ein Sof that are above Atzilus are all included in the aspect of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="78">and it is the matter of one hundred years,</t>
    <t s="79">and as explained in the Zohar</t>
    <t s="80">on the verse</t>
    <t s="81">“And the life of Sarah were one hundred years,”</t>
    <t s="82">that “one hundred years” is the aspect of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="83">the place that includes everything, the supernal place,</t>
    <t s="84">the ten Sefiros, as each one includes ten,</t>
    <t s="85">this is the matter of one hundred years.</t>
    <t s="86">But nevertheless, even Kesser is included in the worlds, and although it is the aspect of the transcendent (Sovev), nevertheless even the transcendent has a connection to the worlds in the aspect of “encompassing” at least,</t>
    <t s="87">therefore it is called “encompassing all worlds.”</t>
    <t s="88">However, the matter of “eternal love” from the term “eternity” is from the perspective of the Atzmus, which is without limit,</t>
    <t s="89">which is above even the aspect of one hundred years,</t>
    <t s="90">and in general it is the matter of the ten Sefiros in the Ma'atzil (the Emanator),</t>
    <t s="91">the hidden ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="92">that from the perspective of this aspect, it is an eternal love.</t>
    <t s="93">However, the matter of “Blessed is Hashem, the God of Israel, from the world and until the world” means that one must draw down from the most supernal world until the lowest world,</t>
    <t s="94">so that it be felt how everything is one,</t>
    <t s="95">and like the language of the maamar,</t>
    <t s="96">“roof and floor literally one.”</t>
    <t s="97">And this is the two interpretations of “eternal love,”</t>
    <t s="98">“olam” in its simple sense, which is this physical world, for Scripture does not depart from its simple meaning,</t>
    <t s="99">and in the world in its simple sense, the drawing down of the aspect of “olam” from the term “eternity.”</t>
    <t s="100">And it is as stated above, that the aspect of “I am Hashem, I have not changed,”</t>
    <t s="101">the absence of change and that which is above changes,</t>
    <t s="102">which is the Atzmus above all lights,</t>
    <t s="103">for in every aspect of light there is change,</t>
    <t s="104">behold, the drawing down of the aspect of “I am Hashem, I have not changed” is specifically in this lowest world and in the future to come.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
